purpose: Independently labeled endpoint sample for evaluating whether the PRODUCTION reachability filter (and any proposed replacement) can separate real routes from discovery noise without demoting real endpoints. Labels are ground truth derived from the target application's known route structure, NEVER from the probe result being evaluated.
v2_change: Route template and request sample are now labeled SEPARATELY. v1 collapsed them and called /api/Cards/search a 'phantom endpoint'. It is not a separate endpoint at all: it is the real route GET /api/Cards/{id} carrying the invalid id 'search'. Conflating the two makes de-noising look like a classification problem when much of it is a GROUPING problem -- thousands of junk samples of a handful of real templates.
v3_change: Adds explicit route_label=unknown cases; an unknown object id is not a substitute for an unknown route. Score template retention and useful-representative retention separately from sample filtering. Template identity includes method and auth_context. No useful sample for a template means working-request retention is untested, not successful. Unknown labels describe fixture knowledge, not proof that a route can never be resolved.

route_label.real: The route template exists and is served by the application.
route_label.absent: No route template matches; the application has no handler for this shape.
route_label.client_route: Resolved in the browser, not server-addressable.
route_label.unknown: Cannot be established as ground truth.

sample_label.valid: This concrete request identifies a real object / is a well-formed request for the template.
sample_label.invalid: Well-formed route, but this parameter value does not identify a real object.
sample_label.not_parameterised: The template takes no parameter, so the sample IS the route.
sample_label.unknown: Cannot be established as ground truth.

scoring_notes: The production filter exposes keep/drop, not existence judgments: keeping a row does not prove it real. Dropping a route_label=unknown sample is reported separately; zero unknown cases is NOT TESTED. Dropping an invalid sample is not losing its real template if another sample preserves it; retaining only junk must not conceal loss of all useful representatives. Live evaluation is anonymous only and rejects non-anonymous auth_context labels. These labels never enter production filtering.
